text:
Devin: Quick question — Finance asked for a conservative spot savings forecast for Q3. They want a proposed hedged/reserve plan (e.g., 30% on-demand, 70% spot with a 10% buffer) and an expected unit cost + variance for chargeback. Can infra/finops sketch numbers?

Priya: We can do that. FYI last quarter avg spot discount across clouds was ~61% vs on-demand but the variance is nontrivial depending on region and time of day. Need region breakdown.

Sam: Ran a quick sim on historical preemptions — with a 30% spot share and a 10% buffer we hit ~95% availability for batch pipelines. But for latency-sensitive inference the tail latency goes up unless you have fast fallback.

Lina: From oncall signals, us-west2 has more correlated network-induced preemptions during maintenance windows. If you're hedging, mix regions to avoid correlated loss.

Arjun: Proposal: mixed-capacity pool across us-west2 + eu-central1 with a 60/40 capacity split reduces correlated interruption risk and smooths price variance. Also keep a small reserved pool for critical models.

Priya: For chargeback we normally allocate cost per GPU-hour consumed. For spot we add a volatility surcharge to account for interruption handling and ops overhead. Draft effective rate formula:

Sam: Code snippet for the sim and cost calc:
```python
# expected effective cost per GPU-hour
on_demand = 2.50  # $/hr example
spot_discount = 0.58
interruption_premium = 0.08  # ops/latency premium
effective_spot = on_demand * (1 - spot_discount) * (1 + interruption_premium)
```

Devin: Can finops-bot produce a 90d moving average of spot discount by region so we can parametrize the sim?

finops-bot: report ready — 90d averages: us-west2 58%, eu-central1 64%, ap-southeast1 52%. CSV saved at /reports/spot_discount_90d.csv :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Priya: Using us-west2 58% discount & 8% interruption premium, example unit econ:
- on-demand = $2.50/hr
- spot effective ≈ 2.50 * (1 - 0.58) * (1 + 0.08) ≈ $1.12/hr (rounded)
So gross savings ~55% on raw rate but after premium it's ~55% effective. Variance band (90d stddev) is ~±12% in us-west2.

Sam: I'll run a Monte Carlo across spot_discount ~ N(0.58, 0.12) and interruption_premium uniformly sampled [0.04,0.12] and simulate 20/30/50/70/90% spot share scenarios. Will drop results here.

Lina: Ops requirement: define SLA spillover rules. Suggest: if request load spike >50% above baseline for >5m, route new allocations to on-demand reservoirs and notify paging.

Devin: For internal chargeback tiers I'm thinking: Core apps (0-20% spot) — no surcharge; Mixed (20-60%) — 5% risk surcharge; Aggressive (>60%) — 12% surcharge. Comments?

Priya: That split looks reasonable as a starting point. Finance will want the sensitivity table showing net cost vs on-demand under different interruption regimes. Also need allocation examples for Analytics pilot.

Arjun: I'll coordinate the Analytics pilot and set aside a 10% reserved block for their top-critical pipelines. Also recommend a cross-region fallback policy so we don't pay on-demand in same region during correlated outages.

Sam: Putting the sim job on the cluster now — ETA ~8h. Will publish CSV + percentile tables. :thumbsup:

Devin: Thanks all. Priya — can you prepare a one-page for Finance with the unit econ, variance, and the proposed chargeback bands? I'll schedule a 30m sync after the Monte Carlo results.

Priya: Yup — will draft and post by EOD tomorrow.

Sam: Monte Carlo results posted: /results/spot_hedge_montecarlo_1775123456.csv (percentiles, cost by spot-share, failure-mode sensitivity).

Devin: Perfect — will review and loop in Finance.

Lina: FYI I opened an ops ticket to codify the spillover policy: INFRA-4219.

Arjun: Thanks — tagging Analytics PM to kick off pilot.

Devin: Closing thread for now. If you add anything after the Monte Carlo please keep it succinct. :white_check_mark:
